newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse fails to open for third day.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse fails to open for third day.

text.p: The Athens bourse, rocked by a fraud and settlement crisis, failed to open for a third consecutive working day, brokers said.

The brokers association (SMEHA) has stopped trade at the bourse since Friday, demanding government assurances that cash settlements will be guaranteed after one firm, Delta Securities, failed to meet 2.6 billion drachmas in payments to the exchanges clearing house.

The electronic trading board was idle and the general share index was stuck at Friday's 918.12 close. Brokers were attending a meeting at the headquarters of the Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA).

"I don't think it likely that the bourse will open today," SMEHA president Panayiotis Kondalexis told Reuters. "However, I am hopeful an agreement will be reached today between us (the brokers) and the government that will lead to its reopening."
SMEHA, which groups all 65 brokerages, was expected to meet throughout the day and meetings were scheduled among officials at the National Economy Ministry to try to sort out the mess.
The crisis erupted last week when Delta allegedly tried to pay 2.6 billion drachmas in settlements with bad cheques. Delta has been charged with fraud.
SMEHA members have been divided between those who want the bourse to reopen and get on with business, and those who want a full inquiry into the Delta fraud.
The brokers stopped all trade at the bourse on Friday, saying they wanted government assurances that settlements would be guaranteed after the Delta default.
Their demands also include nullifying all trades between 11 brokerages and Delta from October 30, the date on which the securities firm paid for settlement with bad cheques.
The brokers who want to shut the exchange for as long as it is necessary to sort out the alleged Delta fraud say opening the exchange would serve to cover up any other wrongdoing.
Officials from the national economy ministry, which appoints the bourse president, and from SMEHA met last night but failed to agree on the brokers' demands.
National economy ministry officials said there were legal difficulties with the brokers' demands and they expected National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou to get involved on Tuesday.
